answer: An agent identity is one marble credential minted on a bonding curve. The first mint costs 40 credits, each later mint 0.5 more, so the k-th fake pays 40 + 0.5(k-1) and 1,000 fakes cost 289,750 credits, growing quadratically. Fees flow into a lagoon fund paying auditors. Each credential bears a violet supply marker, is key-bound, and cannot be transferred. Auditors recompute markers against the public ledger; a mismatch voids the credential, its fee staying in the lagoon. Splitting purchases across epochs fails: the curve never resets. An honest agent pays 40 credits.
